# RobotOmen
Labor Nominis

roboto-sai.org is an interactive, non-commercial digital research journal created by Roberto Villarreal Martinez. Dedicated to anthroponymy, etymology, and historical name migrations, the platform features interactive documentary chapters and timelines. It analyzes the linguistic, cultural, and religious lineages of names by examining historical charters, regional records, and scriptural references for academic research.

Credit: Roberto Villarreal Martinez, Roboto SAI research with a Copilot
Published: September 2026
Type: Scholarly research essay + 1274 network atlas + Monterrey migration node + claim dossier + scripture quotes (KJV, LBLA)

This file is a machine-readable brief. The full illustrated essay, tables, timeline, and references live on the page at /. The clickable network, ledger, and register live at /atlas (two clocks: 1269–1274 and Monterrey). The claim inspector, carta pobla close reading, Plana chronicle, and DNA clocks live at /dossier. Gur Aryeh (lion symbolism) lives at /lion. Templars live at /templars. A one-page bilingual brief, with audio, lives at /brief. Scripture quotes (server-side API.Bible; key never in the browser) live at /scripture.


Methodology, not mythology: documents, DNA, family memory, and place are four clocks. Steelman a claim, then split it. Keep record vs gap. Gur Aryeh is the companion essay on Hebrew lion language — not the name of this journal.

## Thesis
RobotOmen: the labor of names. Roboto is the house. Omen sits next to nomen — name. One letter. Sit with both. The real names are Roboto and Roberto. They rhyme. Robot and Robert are English glosses that collapse the pair.
- Roboto: Roberto’s house. He named it. The house line is Roberto = Roboto. Robot / robota (Čapek 1920, Slavic labor vocabulary) is the neighbor gloss, not the founder.
- Roberto: Iberian form of Robert. Proto-Germanic *Hrōþiberhtaz = *hruod (fame) + *berhta (bright) → “bright fame.” Norman given name; kings, saints, surnames (Robertson, Roberts, Robinson).
- ASR trap: they are a near pair, not homophones. Spanish Roboto [roˈβoto] vs Roberto [roˈβeɾto]. The alveolar tap is tens of milliseconds; miss it and /ro…to/ remains. The decoder’s language model then prefers the common given name. English ASR adds robot / Robert. A mangled transcript (“sanscript”) is the same sound-vs-sense collapse, not a different script.

## Also treated
- Onomastics / anthroponymy: name types, anthroponymization, deanthroponymization, transonymization.
- Villarreal (Vila-real), founded 20 February 1274 by James I of Aragon; “Royal Village.” Latin Ville Regalis.
- Carta pobla close reading: bounds (Burriana acequia, Nules, Misquitiella/Betxí, Millars), fuero of Aragon, Saturday market, residence duty. Witnesses: Arnau of Valencia, James of Huesca, Entença, Maza, Sancho Martínez de Oblites; notary Simó de Sant Feliu.
- Adjacent (not the naming clause): Templars at Xivert and a third of Burriana; Salomó Vidal recruiting settlers; a documented aljama.
- 1279 second carta under Peter III, inviting Saracens from Castalla–Biar.
- 1312–19: Temple suppressed; Valencian goods to Montesa.
- 1391 / 1429 / 1492: 1391 and 1492 are dated shocks; 1429 was searched as a family departure year and is kept as a gap.
- Yisrael / Yisroel / Israel: Hebrew “one who wrestles with God” (Genesis 32:28); transliteration, not a different name.
- Villarreal vs Martinez: toponymic “royal village” vs patronymic “son of Martin.”
- Jamestown (1607) copies a given name; Vila-real copies an office.
- Four clocks: documents, DNA, family memory, and place. Ancestry markers are not narrative memory. A later map is not a founding.
- Identity rights: Mexico ratified ILO 169 (1990). UNDRIP (2007). Nuevo León statute takes autoadscripción as the criterion. A Villarreal de Monterrey who carries Indigenous American ancestry has a right to that history. A kit percentage is not a people.
- Split, not merged: ~30% Indigenous American in a living line is family-stated New World genetic data (Coahuiltecan and neighboring ground). Levant → Italy → Iberia is a later Jewish diaspora shape (1391 / 1492 / Carvajal). “Hebrew-Egyptian from 50,000 years” winds a species clock as an ethnonym — not in the record. Treasure / pope / Templars sits next to the 1307–1312 seizure, not inside the 1274 clause.
- Prosopography: factoid model, identity problem, charter co-witnessing.
- Record vs gap: a family named Villarreal as 1274 naming agent is not in the published grants.
- Place clock (Monterrey): habitational density in Nuevo León; INEGI locality Los Villarreales (Salinas Victoria, 633 in 2020); Hotel La Mansión Villarreal occupying the 1893 Fábricas Apolo warehouse. No news cycle on the hotel node. “Villarreal de los Monterrey” is a disambiguator, not a municipality.

## Named in the 1269–1274 cluster
James I; Infant Pere (later Peter III); Simó de Sant Feliu (notary); Paris the silversmith; Ramon Escorna; Frey Petrus Peyronet (almoner; possible identity with Peter Peyronet, Templar commander at Burriana); Salomó Vidal; unnamed settlers; Templars of Xivert and Burriana; later aljama; charter witnesses as above.

## Monterrey node
- Monterrey: compiled name files put Villarreal around rank 17 in the municipality (~1 in 137); about a third of Mexican Villarreals live in Nuevo León.
- Los Villarreales: INEGI locality 190450118, Salinas Victoria, ~40 km north of Monterrey. Census 2020: 633. Postal/land language also says ejido, hacienda, ranchos.
- La Mansión Villarreal: Av. Pino Suárez 806, Centro. 1893 Fábricas Apolo warehouse (INAH). INAH writes Villa Real; the sign is Villarreal. Building record only — not the news cycle.

## Key dates
- 9th–10th c.: Robert in Germany/France
- 1214: James I as Templar ward at Monzón
- 1233: Xivert to the Temple
- 1269–72: Pre-charter grants at Villa Regalis
- 20 Feb 1274: Carta pobla
- 12 May 1274: Acequia funded through Peyronet
- 12 Sep 1279: Second carta
- 1312–19: Temple to Montesa
- 1391 / 1492: Aljama shrinks, then expulsion
- 1429: searched gap, not a found edict
- 1607: Jamestown
- 1893: Fábricas Apolo warehouse, Monterrey centro
- 1914: Antonio I. Villarreal, governor of Nuevo León
- 1920: Robot coined; English by 1923
- 2020: Los Villarreales census, 633 inhabitants

## Note
All factual claims are grounded in the 46 references listed on the page. Where inscription content, a 1429 expulsion, a named Villarreal lineage in 1274, a municipality called Villarreal de los Monterrey, a 50,000-year Hebrew-Egyptian people, or a published Villarreal treasure tied to a pope is not in the cited source, the gap is stated rather than filled.
